ledger.claim: The driver never reached the pickup point. His own trace puts him a minimum of 779.93 m from the pin at every fix in the trip (derived.driver_track.min_distance_m, mean 1177.11 m), and POL-NS-02's proximity test returns 0 qualifying in-radius fixes and a longest qualifying run of 0 fixes lasting 0.0 s — far short of the 3 consecutive fixes within the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius that POL-NS-02 requires. POL-NS-01 limb (b) therefore fails and the cancellation fee is not chargeable to the rider.

The 'arrived' marker is false. The trip record stamps arrival at 08:02:14 and the system pushed 'Your driver has arrived' at 08:02:15, but the GPS trace shows the driver at least 779.93 m from the pin throughout — more than the 300 m mark in POL-NS-05 — so that marker does not start the waiting clock. Recomputed from the first qualifying in-geofence fix under POL-NS-02, there is no qualifying fix anywhere in the trip, so POL-NS-05(ii) gives the rider a full refund, pays no driver compensation, and records the trip as a false-arrival event against the driver in the referrals list.

Dwell fails independently of the arrival question. The effective in-geofence dwell is 0.0 s (derived.arrival.accumulated_dwell.longest_run_sec) against the 300 s minimum for a STANDARD pickup, a shortfall of 300.0 s, so under POL-NS-06 the fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full whether or not the rider was present. The only route that could have accumulated dwell, POL-NS-06(i), is unavailable: it requires a traffic advisory that is present and populated, and EV-ADVIS-00201-01 is MISSING (no payload, no advisory on file), so limb (i) cannot be run and no accumulation is possible.

The rider-exonerating clause applies on its own terms. The chat log shows one rider message, sent at 08:05:33 inside the waiting window — 'hello? i dont see any car at 118' — which is a locating statement that she cannot see the vehicle, and it is the last message in the thread: the driver never replied within 120 seconds and trip_record.in_app_calls is empty. The rider's own track places her device a maximum of 24.92 m from the pin across all 122 qualifying fixes at zero speed, well inside the 100 m STANDARD rider presence radius. All three limbs of POL-NS-04 hold, so the fee is refunded in full with no driver compensation payable.

This is not a wrong-entrance or pin-ambiguity case either. POL-NS-03 refunds where the driver waits stationary outside the arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin; the driver's closest approach on the entire trace was 779.93 m, nearly double that ceiling. POL-NS-03 therefore neither rescues the fee nor triggers any goodwill payment — it confirms the driver was not at the pickup location at all, rather than at the wrong face of it.

No driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 pays the driver only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it; here POL-NS-02, POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-06 each displace it, since the driver has no qualifying in-geofence fix and no qualifying dwell. The 80 percent payout of SGD 3.20 on the SGD 4.00 fee is not reached.

The record settles this case and does not need a human reviewer. POL-NS-09(b) escalates only where two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival or dwell and no clause resolves the conflict — here POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-05 resolve it, because the same trace that yields no in-radius fix is what makes the 08:02:14 arrival marker false. The remaining triggers are also clear: rider and driver disputes_with_counterparty_90d are each 0, rider no_show_disputes_30d is 0, and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check is not reached. Escalation would hold the disputed SGD 4.00 rather than return it, and nothing in the evidence warrants that.

On quantum: the fare breakdown itemises a single cancellation_fee of SGD 4.00, with base, distance, time, waiting, platform, surge and ERP lines all at zero, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. That SGD 4.00 reconciles with fee_schedule.resolution_rule — the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee (4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (4.00), a tie won by neither dimension — so the fare line is not defective and the rider's loss is exactly the SGD 4.00 she contests. Under POL-GEN-03 a rider-filed dispute in which POL-NS-01 fails is a FULL_REFUND of the whole contested amount, that is SGD 4.00.

Two of the four limbs of POL-NS-01 are carried by the trip record itself and are not in issue on this brief. The record contains a driver 'arrived' event for this trip at 2026-07-23T08:02:14+08:00 (limb (a)), and it shows the trip terminated by the driver at 08:09:40+08:00 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW and no boarding event (limb (d)). The record's own waiting clock between those two timestamps is 7 minutes 26 seconds, entered as trip_record.wait_time_min 7.4, above the 300-second minimum in the fee schedule for a STANDARD pickup.

I will not overstate the GPS, because it is the point on which this fee turns against the driver. The derived arrival facts record 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes and a longest qualifying run of 0.0 seconds, and derived.driver_track puts the driver's closest recorded approach to the pickup pin at about 780 m. That is outside the 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD zone and outside the three-consecutive-fix proximity test that POL-NS-02 requires, so limb (b) of POL-NS-01 cannot be carried on this trace; and because the driver was more than 300 m from the pin at 08:02:14, the arrival marker is a false marker under POL-NS-05 and does not start the waiting clock.

The wrong-entrance route does not save the fee either, and I do not press it. A closest recorded approach of about 780 m is well outside the 400 m ceiling in POL-NS-03, and trip_record.registered_pickup_points is 1, so the pin-ambiguity goodwill that POL-NS-03(ii) provides only where two or more pickup points are registered is not available to this driver on this record.

What the profile evidence does establish is that this is not a fee-farming driver, and no abuse finding is open on either side. driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 3, below the figure of 4 that the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check requires, and 3 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 96 is a rate of 0.031, below the 0.08 rate test, so that check does not trip; with rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d at 0 and both parties' disputes_with_counterparty_90d at 0, neither limb (c) nor limb (d) of POL-NS-09 is engaged.

ruling.explanation:
Rider — the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee charged for trip TRP-00201 is refunded to you in full. Driver — you receive no compensation, because the no-show fee was never chargeable.

What decides the case is the GPS trace. A no-show fee stands only if all four conditions in POL-NS-01 hold. Two do: the trip record contains an 'arrived' event for this trip (08:02:14), and the driver terminated it at 08:09:40 with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW and no boarding event. The other two do not. The trace records 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes and the driver's closest recorded approach to the Blk 118 Rivervale Dr pin was 779.93 m (mean 1,177.11 m), against a STANDARD arrival radius of 50 m — so limb (b) fails. The effective in-geofence dwell is 0.0 s against the 300 s minimum, a shortfall of 300 s — so limb (c) fails too. The trip record's own 7.4-minute clock does not save the fee: that clock runs from the 08:02:14 arrival marker, and at that moment the trace puts the driver more than 779 m from the pin, past the 300 m line in POL-NS-05. The marker is therefore FALSE, it never started the waiting clock, and the clock recomputed from the first qualifying in-geofence fix is zero. Because there is no qualifying in-geofence fix anywhere in the trip, POL-NS-05(ii) refunds the fee in full, pays the driver nothing, and records a false-arrival event against him — that is the referral below.

POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06 reach the same result independently: no qualifying in-radius fix in the 15 minutes before cancellation, and a 300 s dwell shortfall. POL-NS-06(i) cannot accumulate any dwell because the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00201-01 is MISSING (no payload, weight 0.0); it carries no fact and is citable only for its absence, so it neither exonerates the driver nor triggers escalation.

The rider is also exonerated under POL-NS-04: her message at 08:05:33, 'hello? i dont see any car at 118', falls inside the waiting window; the driver neither replied within 120 seconds nor made any in-app call before cancelling; and her device stayed within 24.92 m of the pin across all 122 qualifying fixes, well inside the 100 m STANDARD presence radius.

POL-NS-03 does not apply: the 400 m wrong-entrance ceiling is exceeded, and registered_pickup_points is 1, so no pin-ambiguity goodwill arises. POL-NS-07 pays the driver nothing because POL-NS-01 is not satisfied in full; the anti-farming check it names does not trip either (no_show_terminations_30d = 3, below 4, and 3 / 96 = 0.031, below 0.08), and no adverse finding rests on any context-only profile field.

No escalation: the trip record's arrival marker and the trace conflict on arrival, but POL-NS-05 is the clause that resolves precisely that conflict by declaring the marker false; no artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d) (10 s fix cadence, no gaps, 2 chat messages matching the trip record, and the SGD 4.00 cancellation line equals the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee of 4.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee of 4.00); and the remaining POL-NS-09 limbs are clear. Confidence is 0.90, above the 0.70 floor. Figures used: cancellation_fee SGD 4.00 (fare breakdown EV-FARE-00201), refund SGD 4.00, driver compensation SGD 0.00.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-NS-05(ii): record trip TRP-00201 as a false-arrival event against driver DRV-01590 in the false-arrival record
